title: Safety of sedation in gastrointestinal endoscopy: non-inferiority of safety in ESA (Endoscopic Sedation Assessment) Class A versus ASA (American Society of Anesthesiologists) patients 2 - Validation of a new classification for the assessment of sedation-associated risk in gastrointestinal endoscopy: The ESA (endoscopic sedation risk assessment) classification
summary: More than 7 million gastrointestinal endoscopies are performed in Germany every year.  The vast majority of patients receive sedation during the procedure, i.e. sleep-inducing medication is administered to make the examination comfortable for the patient. There is no doubt that sedation is associated with a certain, albeit low, risk of complications. In view of the risk of complications, a risk assessment prior to the examination is essential.  The ProSed2 study published by our working group was able to show that the risk of sedation-associated complications depends not only on the patient's pre-existing conditions, but also to a large extent on the type and duration of the planned procedure. The aim of the ProSed4 study is to validate a new classification for pre-interventional risk assessment with regard to the occurrence of sedation-associated complications (the ESA classification) in order to be able to quantify the risk more precisely in advance and to set up personnel in accordance with the risk profile.

interventions.name: Observational study/single-arm: Type and incidence of sedation-associated complications in relation to the established risk classification (ASA) compared to the new classification (ESA)

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Sedation in GI endoscopy, ESA A, consent present
Exclusion criteria:
Pregnancy, breastfeeding, lack of consent, lack of capacity to consent, ASA 1, ESA B, emergency endoscopy
